messages.subject_clean: What is the corresponding linear mixed model?
messages.body_plain:
We have the big changes of model between v2 (based on Chang 2012, Clough 2009, 2012) and v3 (method for v3 is under the revision).
There are several videos to explain the model in v3 (https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCnbUMFlIRLaY7fwfSintWuQ).

Briefly, dataProcess function performs log2 transform, normalization, impute for feature-level intensity, summarize for protein-level intensity. Please use summaryMethod='TMP' in dataProcess. (summaryMethod='linear' does not mean linear model for inference, but means mean-based protein-level summarization.) groupComparison for inference in whole plot. Now, we use only Group, Subject variables in the linear mixed-effect model, depending on the experimental design.

HTH
- Meena

messages.body_plain:
there are big changes of models between v2 and v3. We found that models in v2 have many false positives and potentially overfitted in many cases. We proposed the new models in v3 (under the revision). Now, v3 has fewer significant proteins. But, we confirmed that v3 doesn't lose TP and it has much better performance in terms of TP, FP, PPV.
If the number of bio replicate is small (less than 3 per group) and data has bigger variation, MSstats might not report significant proteins.

HTH
- Meena

messages.body_plain:
Dear Veronique,

The method are available in the manuscript, under the revision. Hope that we can share all details soon.
In brief, MSstats summarizes the intensities per label and run, first :

Then, summarized endogenous log intensities are adjusted with respect to their reference counterparts, using the following linear combination of the estimates :

The adjustment equalizes the median of summarized reference log intensities across runs, and shifts the summarized log intensities of the endogenous features in the same run by the same amount.
These adjusted endogenous log intensities are available in x$Runleveldata in v3 or x$ProteinLevelData in v4. (There is no group=0 or subject=0 available in x$Runleveldata in v3 or x4ProteinLevelData in v4.) MSstats uses adjusted endogenous log intensities for inference.

Hope that it helps.
- Meena

messages.body_plain:
Hello,

After summarization and normalization with dataProcess in MSstats, I am visually exploring the distribution of normalized intensities between runs.

I find the difference between 1. output of the dataProcessPlots(type = "QCPlot" , which.protein = 'allonly') and 2. the visualization of mean normalized abundances with ggplot quite intriguing.

The ones that I generated using ggplot were based on:

1. The ProteinLevelData object from the dataProcess output.
2. The summarize mean abundance of the 'newAbundance' values by Protein and Run; from the FeatureLevelData object from the dataProcess output.

Do you have any idea why my boxplots look so different from the QC plot from the dataProcessPlots?

In my boxplots, the data does not look median-centered but in the MSstats QCplots it does.

Many thanks in advance!

Best,
Miguel

The code to generate the boxplots with ggplot:

This gets the data from the ProteinLevelData
quant_annotated <- left_join(msstatstmt_summ_normalized$ProteinLevelData,
                             simple_annotation, by = c("originalRUN")) %>%
          mutate(Cond_Biorep = paste0(Condition, "_", originalRUN, "_", parse_number(batch))) %>%
          filter(!is.na <http://is.na>(GROUP))

This gets the data from the FeatureLevelData and then runs the summarization
quant_annotated_2 <- left_join(msstatstmt_summ_normalized$FeatureLevelData,
                             simple_annotation,
                             by = c("originalRUN")) %>%
  filter(!is.na <http://is.na>(GROUP)) %>%
  group_by(PROTEIN, Condition, batch, originalRUN) %>%
  summarise(Norm_abundance = mean(newABUNDANCE, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  mutate(Norm_abundance = ifelse(is.nan(Norm_abundance),
                                 yes = NA,
                                 no = Norm_abundance),
         Cond_Biorep = paste0(Condition, "_", originalRUN, "_", parse_number(batch)))

qcplot <- ggplot(quant_annotated,
                 mapping = aes(x = Cond_Biorep,
                               y = LogIntensities,
                               fill = Condition)) +
          geom_boxplot() +
          scale_y_continuous(limits = c(5, 40)) +
          facet_grid(.~Condition, scales = "free") +
          theme(axis.text.x = element_text(hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.1, size = 10, angle = 90),
                axis.text.y = element_text(hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.1, size = 10),
                panel.background = element_blank(),
                panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey"),
                panel.border = element_rect(colour = "black", fill=NA, size=1.5),
                axis.title=element_text(size=12,face="bold"))

qcplot2 <- ggplot(quant_annotated_2,
                 mapping = aes(x = Cond_Biorep,
                               y = Norm_abundance,
                               fill = Condition)) +
          geom_boxplot() +
          scale_y_continuous(limits = c(5, 40)) +
          facet_grid(.~Condition, scales = "free") +
          theme(axis.text.x = element_text(hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.1, size = 10, angle = 90),
